page.layout: One printed page. Top: running head with page number 120 at the left. Below it, one column of Latin verse in italic, stanzas set with indented alternate lines. A horizontal rule follows. Below the rule: the heading "XXII. GAL." centred, then one column of French verse in roman, with a large initial C. At the bottom right: catchword "La". Faint mirrored text in the right margin is show-through and is left out.

p.i: Quo te, stulte, rapit fuga. Velox præcipitem? Siste, precor, gradum: Et Virtutis Olympicæ Tandem verba pio pectore connota. Ah! non audit, & impotens Virtutem reicit surdior Adria, Illum quum Nothus excitat, Aut rauca Æolijs murmura flatibus Nubes tollit ad arduas. Ah! vitæ propero persequitur breuis Cursu gaudia feruidus. Ceu quum monte ferox vnda ruit: simul Ingens imber ab æthere Nimboso cecidit. Quid? Sapientiæ Spernit consilium sacræ. Sic ripas fluuius diluuie tumens Vasta negligit, & vago Moles oppositas diruit impetu.

main_text.head: XXII. GAL.
main_text.p: C'EST vn arbre que le Monde, Dont la racine profonde Iusques aux enfers attaint. De verd le fueillage est paint. La fleur est plaisante & belle. Le fruict suit de pres la fleur.

page.notes: The running head is printed as two lines, "DE MVNDI" above "LAT.", combined here. The XXII. GAL. line is set apart above a rule and treated as a small heading. Faint mirrored text in the right margin is show-through from the reverse and is not transcribed. No doubtful readings.
